description:
A field access on a known `opaque resource` receiver, for a field the resource
cannot have, is silently widened to `any` at semantic analysis and reaches the
backend. Interp reports a step-evaluation failure; JIT and AOT ABORT THE HOST
PROCESS inside the runtime. No diagnostic is emitted on any path.

## Repro

    defmodule R do
      @type t :: opaque resource(integer)
      fn unwrap(h), do: h.value
      fn bad(h), do: h.foo
    end

    extern "C" fn fz_resource_test_print_dtor(integer) :: nil
    fn dwrap(x), do: fz_resource_test_print_dtor(x)

    fn main() do
      a = make_resource(10, &dwrap/1)
      dbg(R.unwrap(a))
      dbg(R.bad(a))
    end

    interp: 10
            fz2 interp: backend executable 8 function 68 entry 0 step evaluation
            failed: StructField: subject is not a map or Struct     (exit 1)

    run:    10
            thread 'main' panicked at runtime/src/ir_runtime.rs:1654:10:
            fz_struct_get_named_field_ref: ExpectedTag { expected: ValueKind(3),
            found: ValueKind(7) }                                   (exit 134)

    build:  same panic and exit 134 from the built binary.

## Root

src/compiler2/jobs/semantic.rs:469-477. `LoweredStep::FieldAccess` asks
`Types::map_field_lookup` and, on `None`, does `.unwrap_or_else(|| any_ty(world))`
-- discarding a PROVEN impossibility while the settled receiver type and the
field-access span are both still authoritative.

A known resource has the language-defined `.value` projection subject to opaque
visibility; `h.foo` is not a dynamic struct lookup, so widening it to `any` is
not conservatism, it is losing a fact.

## Strategy

At semantic field resolution, separate a receiver domain that PROVES the field
impossible from a genuinely unknown map/struct field set. Emit one stable
diagnostic carrying the field-access span for the impossible case, and keep the
conservative `any` only for receivers whose settled domain can still admit an
unknown field. The runtime `expect` in `fz_struct_get_named_field_ref`
(runtime/src/ir_runtime.rs:1639, expect at :1654) then stays an unreachable
compiler-invariant guard rather than a user-reachable abort.

## Checks

- The probe is rejected identically by interp, run and build, BEFORE backend
  execution, with the same diagnostic code and span.
- `R.unwrap(a)` keeps printing 10 -- `.value` remains the payload projection.
- These stay green: matrix::resource_lifecycle, matrix::file_handle,
  matrix::file_resource_lifecycle, matrix::a-resource_aot_dtor (all pass at
  HEAD).
- Full lib + matrix green.

Old ticket was substantively accurate; only drift: the widening site is
jobs/semantic.rs:469-477, and the interp error text is
`StructField: subject is not a map or Struct`.
title: Reject an impossible resource field access at the semantic boundary instead of widening it to any
